messages.author: 8bb087a769327765
messages.subject: Summarizing occupancy across multiple sites
parts:
Hi All,

I am running a multi-species occupancy model with covariates in a Bayesian framework. In the structure of my model, I am generating and estimate for occupancy (e.g.) for each species and site, as follows:

logit(occupancy[species, site]) <- occupancy_intercept[species] + inprod(occupancy_coef[species, 1:n_covs], occupancy_covariates[site, 1:n_covs])

We are interested in making a statement about species-specific occupancies across the whole set of sites (i.e, the study-level occupancy for each species) with credible intervals. I've come up with a few options, but can't find and example for that verifies correct way to do this, if there is one.

Thanks for your help!

Kelly

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: Summarizing occupancy across multiple sites
parts:
Hi Kelly,

If you save the posterior draws for the latent states (e.g., z[i,j] for species i at site j) you should be able to generate any relevant summaries and compute credible intervals. I think the quantiles of mean(z[i,]) across all iterations provides what you need here. It'll turn your model output into a huge object depending on the dimensions but it gives you flexibility for derived estimates.

-Dan

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: Summarizing occupancy across multiple sites
parts:
Dear Kelly,

 

Do this based on the estimates of the site-specific presence-absence indicatzors z. The occupancy proportion in the sample of sites is sum(z) / number of sites. You can monitor that as a derived quantity and then get a posterior distribution for that.

 

Best regards  --- Marc
